memory_candidates.content: On this NixOS host, `~/.config/pip/pip.conf` sets `install.user=true` globally (a `user` pip config setting is picked up outside any project's control). This silently breaks `pip install` inside a freshly-created Python venv with 'Can not perform a --user install. User site-packages are not visible in this virtualenv.' The fix is NOT to edit the user's pip.conf (out of scope for a repo-scoped task) but to override per-invocation with `PIP_USER=0` env var plus `--no-user` on every `pip install` call while working inside that venv.

`nix develop` (and `nix-shell`) assigns a fresh, non-persisting TMPDIR on every separate shell invocation — it appends a new `nix-shell.XXXXXX` subdirectory to whatever TMPDIR was passed in, and this suffix changes each time `nix develop` starts. Combined with the fact that each Bash tool call in this harness is a brand-new shell (exported env vars do not persist across calls), any multi-step NixOS-safe rehearsal (create venv -> install tools -> build -> check -> compare) MUST run as a single script inside ONE `nix develop --command bash /path/to/script.sh` invocation. Splitting the steps across multiple Bash tool calls silently loses the venv/tmp state between calls.

Canonical GitHub Actions job graph for PyPI Trusted Publishing (OIDC), replacing a long-lived PYPI_API_TOKEN: a `build` job (runs once, `python -m build` + `twine check --strict`, then `actions/upload-artifact`) feeds two OIDC publish jobs via `actions/download-artifact` — `publish-testpypi` (`environment: testpypi`, `permissions: id-token: write`, `repository-url: https://test.pypi.org/legacy/`, `continue-on-error: true` so an unconfigured/failing TestPyPI rehearsal never blocks production) and `publish-pypi` (`environment: pypi`, `permissions: id-token: write`, default PyPI). Both use `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1` with `skip-existing: true`. Top-level workflow `permissions` should be scoped to `contents: read`, with each job granting only the extra permission it needs (`id-token: write` for the two publish jobs, `contents: write` for a final GitHub-Release-creation job).
